correctness.rationale: The exact stationary backward run-weight sum has nonnegative disjoint weights totalling at most one. Conditional spherical pair orthogonality proves the 2/d L2 bound. Independent exponential backward ages give two beta attenuation factors and a unique contractive perpetuity. An upper-tail sandwich plus negligible near-unit feedback proves exponent mu/b and the constant. A lower-tail negative-moment bootstrap yields a finite inverse moment for every lambda/(2b), enabling exact beta-product tail asymptotics. The stationary mean matches an independent velocity-covariance calculation, and standard-library numerical diagnostics corroborate the formulas. The proof is analytic and is not based on finite simulation alone.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary paper establishes the stochastic model and all fixed-dimensional coordinate moments, and its high-order boundary exponent concerns one coordinate. The precise random squared-radius limit, its nonasymptotic L2 error and two sharp rate-dependent edge constants are not claimed there. A 2026 Kesten treatment concerns a model without a finite resting phase. The 2019 three-state RTP is low-dimensional. A broad generalized beta-perpetuity theorem could subsume parts and remains a documented external priority risk.
residual_risks: Specialized general perpetuity/small-ball literature may already imply the beta-discount tail asymptotic in another formulation.
Existing complete moment recurrence formally determines compactly supported marginal laws; publication priority of any particular singular high-dimensional limit requires expert confirmation.
2019 lower-dimensional article was not fully reconstructed beyond accessible material; its model and scope differ from the all-dimensional statement.

value.rationale: The high-dimensional radial observable remains randomly distributed despite vanishing inner products between different headings. The two opposite rare-event regimes have independent physical mechanisms and sharp exact rate exponents and prefactors. Identifying the squared-mass perpetuity and finite negative moments moves beyond simply computing fixed moments and yields a motivated, reusable boundary classification. The result does not claim more than the separately ordered limits and lacks a full density formula.
